finding_key: packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts::`docx_alignments` lookup is not actually closed — prototype keys (`tostring`, `constructor`, `__proto__`, `valueof`) resolve to inherited values that get interpolated into `w:jc/@w:val`
evidence: Verified in packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts: `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` is a plain object literal and `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS[style.alignment as string] ?? 'left'` consults the prototype chain, so `style.alignment === 'toString'` yields `Object.prototype.toString`, which survives the `??` and `!== 'left'` checks and is stringified into `<w:jc w:val="function toString() { [native code] }"/>`; `'__proto__'` yields `[object Object]`. The same pattern exists in packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts (`ALGN[block.style.alignment] ?? 'l'`). This breaks the code's own "closed lookup / fail-closed" claim for values the PR itself treats as untrusted CRDT data, though impact is limited: only Object.prototype key names trigger it, and the inherited values' string forms contain no quotes, so it produces a schema-invalid attribute value rather than an injection escape.
